To assemble a sample, RiboPilot needs a reference database of
rDNA sequences from closely related organisms. This step groups samples and
builds one database from GenBank per group, which can be reused across projects.

To start, click **Propose groups**. RiboPilot automatically groups samples that can share a database.
For the test project samples it proposes three groups. The red line warns that one of them,
Actinopteri (all ray-finned fishes), holds more records than the usual maximum:

![Proposed reference groups for the test samples](figures/get-started/reference-propose.png)

Click **Apply** to accept the proposed groups. 

You should now see a **Groups** table. Tick all three groups and
click **Set up database** at the end of any ticked row. The window offers
**Download sequences from GenBank**, **Use a database I already have**, and
**Leave these samples on their current database**. With only a single group ticked,
it also offers **Change which clade this group uses**:

![The choices for setting up a group's reference database](figures/get-started/reference-setup.png)

Choose **Download sequences from GenBank** and press **Run
from App**. The choice applies to every ticked group, so one run builds all
three databases. 

::: {.alert .alert-hydra}
[HYDRA]{.hydra-tag} **Submit as job.** Press **Submit as job** in place of
**Run from App**; see [Submit a run as a job](Clusters.html#submit-a-run-as-a-job).
The app connects each database to the project once the job finishes.
:::

When done, every group's Status should read **Ready**:

![Reference groups with their databases ready](figures/get-started/reference-ready.png)

In our test, the Syngnathiformes database (about 10,500 GenBank records) took
under 3 minutes and Pleuronectiformes (about 2,300 records) under 1 minute.
Actinopteri holds about 43,000 records, so its download takes much longer.

When working with your own samples, see
[Reference databases](Reference-Databases.html) for more details.
